historical_attempts.raised_from: RedactingJsonRpcTransport.post_json() (scripts/run_b2n_p3c_migration_lineage_run.py), which increments self.physical_request_count BEFORE calling urllib.request.urlopen() and catches HTTPError/URLError/OSError/ValueError to redact the credential-bearing URL from the exception message
historical_attempts.implication: physical_request_count on the transport object was incremented to at least 1 before this exception was raised, meaning network dispatch was very likely attempted (an HTTPError specifically indicates the server responded with a non-2xx status, which requires the request to have actually reached Helius and gotten a response -- not merely a connection failure)
historical_attempts.reason_no_ledger_entry: the exception is raised and propagates out of post_json() -> MigrationGetTransactionAdapter.acquire_once() -> B2NExecutor.run()'s self.client.acquire_once(mint=...) call (line 217) before the code ever reaches self.ledger.append(entry) at line 244
historical_attempts.exact_physical_request_count_consumed: UNKNOWN -- not deterministically recoverable from any artifact; the transport object and its physical_request_count counter existed only in that process's memory and were never persisted anywhere

historical_attempts.root_cause: MigrationGetTransactionAdapter (src/acquisition/b2w_projection.py) never exposes a provider_request_count attribute. B2NExecutor.run() reads `before = getattr(self.client, 'provider_request_count', 0)` and `after = getattr(self.client, 'provider_request_count', before)` against self.client, which is the ADAPTER, not the transport -- so both getattr calls silently fall back to their defaults (0 and before, respectively) on every call, making delta ALWAYS equal 0 regardless of what actually happened on the wire. Separately, OneRequestResponse.provider_request_count defaults to 1, and MigrationGetTransactionAdapter never overrides it on any return path (SUCCESS, RPC_ERROR, or MALFORMED_RESPONSE all return the default). Therefore request_count (1) != delta (0) on EVERY invocation, deterministically, regardless of whether the underlying HTTP call succeeded, failed, or was never reached.
historical_attempts.implication: this is a deterministic CODE defect, not an intermittent live/network condition -- it would fire identically on every future attempt using the current MigrationGetTransactionAdapter + B2NExecutor pairing as-is, success or failure, until repaired
historical_attempts.reason_no_ledger_entry: same as attempt 1: the exception is raised before self.ledger.append(entry) at line 244 is ever reached
historical_attempts.exact_physical_request_count_consumed: UNKNOWN for the same reason as attempt 1 -- BUT given the root cause is deterministic and independent of the HTTP outcome, it is likely (not certain) that a real network dispatch occurred on this attempt too, since RedactingJsonRpcTransport.post_json() increments its counter and calls urlopen() BEFORE any exception related to the counter-mismatch bug could possibly be raised (the counter-mismatch check happens entirely inside B2NExecutor.run(), after acquire_once() has already returned)

authorization_reuse_recommendation.reasoning: the old authorization (run_id b2n-p3b-c39499f523e42083ce045d70, max_physical_requests=20) has an unknown, non-zero number of physical requests already consumed against it with zero durable evidence; continuing to use the SAME run_id and the SAME max_physical_requests=20 ceiling without accounting for the historical attempts would allow up to 20 NEW requests on top of an unknown number of PRIOR requests, silently exceeding the intended 20-total-request bound for this authorization's lifetime
authorization_reuse_recommendation.action_taken_this_milestone: durability defect repaired; a fresh authorization/run_id was created (see repair_and_fresh_authorization below) rather than resuming under the compromised run_id

root_cause_fix.mechanism: wraps MigrationGetTransactionAdapter; before delegating to the adapter, durably appends an ATTEMPT_RESERVED event to a new PreDispatchEventLedger; tracks provider_request_count by diffing the TRANSPORT's own counter before/after the call (the object that actually dispatches), not the adapter (which never exposed one); forces the returned OneRequestResponse.provider_request_count to match what was actually observed, eliminating the always-1-vs-always-0 mismatch that caused B2N_CLIENT_REQUEST_COUNTER_MISMATCH on every prior invocation
root_cause_fix.event_ledger_semantics: append-only, multiple immutable events permitted per ordinal (ATTEMPT_RESERVED then a terminal event), unlike B2NAttemptLedger's single-terminal-entry-per-ordinal design; no UPDATE is ever performed
root_cause_fix.canonical_counter: physical_requests_attempted() counts an ordinal once network dispatch was attempted (a terminal ATTEMPT_SUCCEEDED or ATTEMPT_FAILED event exists), regardless of HTTP outcome; ATTEMPT_NOT_DISPATCHED (exception before the transport call) does not count
root_cause_fix.reproduction_test: tests/test_b2n_p3e_accounting_repair.py::test_reproduces_original_counter_mismatch_defect_with_real_adapter (confirms the ORIGINAL unwrapped wiring still fails exactly as observed live) and test_durable_accounting_client_fixes_the_mismatch (confirms the wrapped wiring succeeds)
root_cause_fix.scenario_coverage: tests/test_b2n_p3e_accounting_repair.py scenarios A-F (HTTP success, RPC error, timeout, malformed response, transport exception after dispatch, exception before dispatch) all pass with correct accounting and zero real network calls
